summary:
We developed GÉNESIS, an interactive educational video game designed to help children and young people understand how NASA space missions work, in a fun and immersive way. The project allows users to explore environments inspired by the lunar surface and engage in activities based on the Apollo 11 and Apollo 15 missions.

In the Apollo 11 segment, players learn about key elements such as the moon landing, spacewalks, the collection of lunar samples, and the deployment of scientific instruments. In the Apollo 15 segment, they can explore the use of the lunar rover and discover the importance of studying the Moon’s rocks and terrain. In this way, the video game transforms scientific and historical concepts into interactive, easy-to-understand challenges.

Our project also explores the creative use of artificial intelligence throughout the development process—from conceptualizing scenarios and mechanics to designing the visual and educational experience. GÉNESIS addresses a significant need: many people are only familiar with space missions through text or static images. With this video game, students can visualize and explore these missions, learning through active participation.
details: GÉNESIS is a 3D educational video game that allows children and young people to explore how NASA space missions work in a fun, visual, and interactive way. The project recreates challenges inspired by Apollo 11 and Apollo 15, in which players can traverse the lunar surface, collect rock samples, set up scientific instruments, explore the lunar module, and drive a rover. Furthermore, it incorporates immersive experiences—featuring official 360° NASA videos—to bring users closer to real-world scenarios, technologies, and training related to space exploration. The game aims to facilitate the understanding of concepts such as lunar gravity, regolith, spacewalks, seismographs, and scientific exploration—topics that can sometimes be difficult to visualize through text or static images alone. Its development involved the use of React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Tailwind CSS, alongside artificial intelligence tools to assist with ideation, design, and content creation. The project’s innovation lies in its integration of video games, history, science, virtual reality, and learning into a single platform. Its intended impact is to spark curiosity about astronomy, programming, and STEM careers, providing an accessible tool for schools, science fairs, and students who wish to learn through active participation.
